p1.fix: last_closing_line() answers, in one scan before classifying, whether any later line carries a closing marker. Fence markers are removed from the evidence a note contributes, so a fenced block reaches the model as ordinary prose. The system prompt still declares all evidence untrusted, so no trust boundary changes.

findings.what: _RULE_LINE_RE does not implement Markdown thematic breaks exactly, in both directions
findings.witness_a: '* * *' is a valid thematic break (Markdown permits spaces between identical markers) and is KEPT as content
findings.witness_b: '    ---' at four spaces of indent is NOT a thematic break (breaks allow at most three leading spaces) and is DELETED
findings.executor_note: both are PRE-EXISTING, not regressions. The base pattern '^[ \t]*[-=_*]{3,}[ \t]*$' has the identical behaviour on both witnesses - it cannot match across the spaces in '* * *', and its '[ \t]*' accepts unlimited indent. P2 changed only the mixed-marker case, which it fixed correctly ('-=_*' now survives). So P2 neither introduced nor repaired these two.
findings.test_gap: the suite's break checks cover only contiguous runs, so neither witness is pinned
